title: Organiser guide
text: Set up, run and finish a tournament without technical knowledge.

title: Organiser guide · Organiser guide
text: # Organiser guide  J3 lets a non-technical organiser create, run and finish a tournament from one browser. Use the seeded local demo to try every role before your event.

title: Organiser guide · Before you start
text: Have your event name, dates, venue, logo/banner, disciplines, categories and rules ready. You do not need federation rule files: J3 asks plain-language questions and supplies presets.

title: Organiser guide · Open the demo
text: Run `bun run dev`, sign in as the seeded admin (`j3@local` or any account on `/demo-accounts`, password `demo`). The J3 icon always returns to `/public`; nav stays visible on every normal route. Use **↗ New tab** only when a board needs its own TV/projector screen.

title: Organiser guide · Create your event in five steps
text: 1. **Event & identity** — name, dates, venue, branding, preset or template. 2. **Disciplines & rules** — timings, points, rounds and style per discipline. 3. **Categories & constraints** — age, weight, height, belt, gender, caps and split/merge rules. 4. **People & invitations** — invite officials and club owners; fighters self-register. 5. **Review & launch** — validation jumps to the offending s

title: Organiser guide · Invite clubs and register fighters
text: Admins invite runners/admins; runners invite officials and club owners; club owners invite only their own fighters/spectators. Invites return a `/invite/<token>` link that works before email/SMS is connected. Fighters choose a compatible division, club or independent status, and a belt from the colour picker. Full/incompatible categories are greyed out.  | Role | Invites | Main job | |---|---|---|

title: Organiser guide · Let J3 build the draw
text: The readiness checklist runs eligibility, balanced pools, same-club spread, BYEs, seeding, official assignments and format fallback to round robin for small pools. Drag fighters or match order to override; every round keeps a copy of each fighter for full history.

title: Organiser guide · Score a contest
text: Officials open `/official` or the mat console, select their assigned bout, log techniques from the catalogue, award cards, run the authoritative clock and confirm Red/Blue/Draw. Points come from the event rule snapshot, so a browser cannot invent scores. Results lock with a recorded undo path.

title: Organiser guide · Kata and training
text: Kata uses numbered shitei/tokuyi rounds, panel judging with high/low dropped, bunkai scores and automatic advancement. Training sessions and fair sparring rotation are available without changing the competition draw.

title: Organiser guide · Screens and displays
text: Open `/public`, `/display`, `/brackets`, `/tables`, `/pools`, `/control` or `/view` on separate screens. The control room switches views in place; displays have their own URLs for TVs and LED walls. Use **Display control** to assign saved dashboard templates to screens.

title: Organiser guide · Keep the event on track
text: The public dashboard has a large clock, next-up callouts and drift-aware projected times. Mark schedule items complete as the day moves; J3 recalculates. PA toasts and browser TTS announce fighters, medals and results.

title: Organiser guide · Dealing with changes on the day
text: For no-shows, injuries, withdrawals or voluntary promotion, record the technical outcome or move the fighter in the draw. J3 rebalances the affected pool/promotion and keeps an audit entry. Small or empty categories get format suggestions instead of broken brackets.

title: Organiser guide · Audit and exports
text: `/audit` shows actor, role, time, target and before/after for every material action. `/data` queries allow-listed tables; CSV export/import and printable brackets/scoresheets are available to authorised users.

title: Organiser guide · Need help?
text: Use **Docs & guides** in `dev.sh`, `/guides` for role-specific hands-on steps, or the API explorer at `/docs/api`. Skipping a guide marks it complete until you explicitly restart it.

title: Accounts & invitations
text: Demo logins, hosted owner bootstrap and the admin-to-participant invite chain.

title: Accounts & invitations · Accounts & invitations
text: # Accounts, roles and invitations  One identity system serves the web app, venue server and native phone build. Authority flows down; privileged actions are audited.

title: Accounts & invitations · Demo and QA sign-in
text: Local/native demo builds seed accounts sharing password `demo`. Use **Demo accounts — one click to test any role** on `/login`, or the searchable list at `/demo-accounts`. Switching mints a real server session for that user, so role guards and private/public boundaries are genuine. `GET /api/v1/demo/credentials` supplies the sheet; the APK bundles it for offline identity switching. Writes still re

title: Accounts & invitations · Hosted owner
text: First hosted boot creates the admin (`j3@local` / `J3 Owner` by default). Override with `J3_OWNER_EMAIL` / `J3_OWNER_NAME`. `J3_OWNER_PASSWORD` wins; otherwise a strong one-time password is printed once in the startup log and `must_change_password` forces a reset at `/login` via `POST /api/v1/auth/password`.

title: Accounts & invitations · Invite chain
text: Public signup creates only fighters and spectators. Everyone else is invited:  | Inviter | May invite | |---|---| | Admin | every role, including other admins | | Runner | officials, club owners, fighters, spectators | | Official | club owners, fighters, spectators | | Club leader | fighters/spectators **in their own club only** |  Create an invite from **Admin → Invite an account** or **Club → In

title: Accounts & invitations · Enforced boundaries
text: - Roles come from the database on every privileged request; client-supplied roles are ignored. - `admin` is stored as a flagged runner but exposed as `admin` in UI, API and audit. - Club owners cannot change tournament templates, permissions or other clubs. - Scoring requires contest assignment (admin/runner override); points remain server-resolved.

title: Runner guide
text: The full event path: create, check in, score, publish and audit.

title: Runner guide · Runner guide
text: # Tournament runner guide  Runners own event setup and day-to-day overrides. Admins can do everything a runner can plus the authority matrix.

title: Runner guide · Before you start
text: Pick a template or clone last year's event. Confirm disciplines, rule snapshots, categories, venue and branding; copy the event URL for each display screen.

title: Runner guide · 1. Create the event
text: Use the five-step wizard: identity/branding → rules → categories → people → review. Validation jumps to the offending step. Launch saves a reusable template and generates pools, brackets, assignments and dashboard views.

title: Runner guide · 2. Check the draw
text: Review balanced pools, same-club spread, BYEs and format fallback. Drag fighters or match order to override; create awards and a medal table once categories are final.

title: Runner guide · 3. Brief your team
text: Assign officials to mats/contests; unassigned corners cannot score. Share `/official` and mat console URLs, the schedule and PA conventions.

title: Runner guide · 4. Check-in and weigh-in
text: Search/check in fighters, record metric weight, and flag out-of-class competitors. Handle no-shows and injuries with a recorded technical outcome that rebalances the pool.

title: Runner guide · 5. Run the mats
text: Monitor `/control` and the public clock. Confirm results, manage promotion and third-place/bronze rules, and trigger PA callouts. Undo or correct any score with an audit entry.

title: Runner guide · 6. Publish and celebrate
text: Open `/public`, `/brackets`, `/tables` and `/medals` on displays. Use the guided ceremony, winner animations and Street Fighter theme where appropriate.

title: Runner guide · After the event
text: Review `/audit`, export CSV/brackets/scoresheets, archive the event and save the setup as a template for next time.

title: Official guide
text: Assignments, corner scoring, penalties, clock and kata panels.

title: Official guide · Official guide
text: # Official & moderator guide  Officials score only contests they are assigned to; runners/admins may override any contest.

title: Official guide · Get assigned
text: Open `/official`. The feed lists your assigned bouts (runners see all). Pair your judge phone via the mat assignment shown in the control room.

title: Official guide · Select the contest and corner
text: Choose the active contest and the first/second corner before scoring. Seeded events default to **Red vs White**; the organiser can change both names and colours per event. The API keeps stable `red`/`blue` scoring slots so results stay deterministic, while every operator surface shows the configured label. Never rely on colour alone.

title: Official guide · Log a technique
text: Search the 400-entry catalogue by English, romaji, Japanese script, style or movement tag. Pick the configured point value; the server resolves points/kind/card/label from the rule snapshot, so the client cannot spoof them. Recent moves appear on the scoreboard.

title: Official guide · Penalties and cards
text: Award yellow/red cards or shido from the configured ladder. Cards show on the correct fighter's side; DQ thresholds follow the event rules.

title: Official guide · Control the clock
text: Start, pause and resume the authoritative mat timer. Pausing on referee stoppage flashes the board; resume only on the scorekeeper's command. Hold/pin timers count down live.

title: Official guide · Technical wins and losses
text: Record injury, forfeit, no-show, withdrawal, referee, cheating or DQ using the fight outcome vocabulary. The bout locks to `forfeit` with an audited technical event and SSE fan-out.

title: Official guide · Submissions and instant wins
text: Tap/verbal submission ends the bout immediately and overrides accumulated points; promotion follows the configured rules.

title: Official guide · Kata panel judging
text: Panel phones submit scores/deductions; the server drops high/low and computes the authoritative total. Shitei/tokuyi rounds, bunkai and advancement are tracked separately.

title: Official guide · Finish the bout
text: Confirm Red/Blue/Draw. Confirmation asks again for major outcomes; results lock and celebrations fire. Hand over any incident notes to the runner.

title: Participant guide
text: Registration, profile, check-in and following your contests.

title: Participant guide · Participant guide
text: # Participant & spectator guide

title: Participant guide · Create your profile
text: Self-register as fighter or spectator. Add photo, contact details, DOB, height/weight (metric or imperial; stored metric), belt/rank, club affiliation or independent status. Minors need guardian consent. Settings hold language, units, appearance and profile data.

title: Participant guide · Register for the right division
text: J3 offers only categories compatible with your stats. Full or incompatible categories are greyed out. A heavier/older division may be offered with explicit consent to move up.

title: Participant guide · Before the day
text: Read the public event details: rules, required kit/protection, times, venue and schedule. Check your schedule and notifications for callouts.

title: Participant guide · At the venue
text: Check in and weigh in at the desk; QR badges identify you. Watch `/public` for "you're up next" and follow your mat/bracket. On phones you only see public, participant and club screens — operator tools stay on larger displays.

title: Participant guide · Results and appeals
text: Results appear on tables and brackets with W/L/D glyphs and outcome codes. Ask your club leader or the runner about corrections; every change is audited.

title: Participant guide · Spectators
text: Spectators see only published data: dashboard, schedule, brackets, tables, pools and public details. No scoring drafts, private notes or personal data are exposed.

title: Frequently asked questions
text: Offline use, categories, scoring, displays and recovery.

title: Frequently asked questions · Frequently asked questions
text: # Frequently asked questions

title: Frequently asked questions · Can I use J3 with no internet at the venue?
text: Yes. The venue server and LAN displays work offline. The Android APK bundles a seeded database and read-only snapshot, so phone screens work even with the server stopped; scoring needs the LAN.

title: Frequently asked questions · Do I need to know federation rules?
text: No. Pick a preset or enter plain-language values; J3 stores per-event rule snapshots. Advanced raw config is optional.

title: Frequently asked questions · Can one fighter enter more than one category?
text: Only if the event's category policy allows it; some disciplines restrict athletes to one age and one weight division.

title: Frequently asked questions · What happens if a category has only two entrants?
text: J3 suggests best-of-three or round robin instead of a broken elimination bracket. Empty categories are flagged, not rendered as invalid matches.

title: Frequently asked questions · How are same-club meetings avoided?
text: Seeding and pool generation spread clubs/countries with controlled randomisation where the rules allow it. Organisers can override with drag-and-drop.

title: Frequently asked questions · Who can change a score?
text: Only an assigned official or an admin/runner override. Every write is attributed, audited and correctable with a recorded undo.

title: Frequently asked questions · How do I put different views on different screens?
text: Each display route has its own URL. Open it in a new tab on the target TV/projector; use Display control to assign saved dashboard templates.

title: Frequently asked questions · Which languages are supported?
text: Eleven locales for shared labels: EN, FR, DE, ES, PT, HI, PA, AR, JA, KO, ZH.

title: Frequently asked questions · Can I restore a tournament after a crash?
text: Yes. SQLite WAL plus a single-file backup allow recovery; restore the database and restart the venue server.

title: Frequently asked questions · Where do I find the raw API contract?
text: See the [API guide](/docs/api-guide) or the interactive API reference at `/docs/api`.

title: Formats & promotion
text: Pools, BYEs, eliminations, bronze rules and history.

title: Formats & promotion · Formats & promotion
text: # Formats, pools & promotion

title: Formats & promotion · Selecting a format
text: Formats follow the event's `FormatPolicy` and actual entrant count. J3 suggests round robin when elimination is impossible, and records the chosen format per stage.

title: Formats & promotion · Round robin
text: Circle-method scheduling gives every fighter the same number of bouts. Standings use the configured ordered tie-break chain, and every pairing appears once.

title: Formats & promotion · Pools
text: Pool generation balances size and skill, seeds by rank/stats and spreads same-club fighters where allowed. Organisers can drag fighters between pools and regenerate with a new random seed.

title: Formats & promotion · Elimination brackets
text: Single and double elimination are both supported, with explicit true-double vs consolation-double semantics. BYEs are allocated by seed/title; first-round club/country separation is configurable.

title: Formats & promotion · Third place and bronze
text: If the two losing semi-finalists have not met, a third-place rematch is scheduled. If they have, two bronze medals are awarded. This is a per-discipline rule.

title: Formats & promotion · Promotion and history
text: Winners/losers/draws advance according to rule config. Each round keeps a copy of the fighter card, so brackets show the full path. Repechage, forfeits and no-shows rebalance affected slots.

title: Formats & promotion · See also
text: Live scoring rules, the official guide and the public brackets display.

title: Live scoring rules
text: Points, holds, submissions, penalties and tie-breaks.

title: Live scoring rules · Live scoring rules
text: # Live scoring rules  Scoring is authoritative on the venue server. Clients send `techniqueId` and optional `pointLabel`; points, kind, card and label are resolved from the event rule snapshot.

title: Live scoring rules · Score events
text: Every point, technique, advantage and move is a timestamped event attributed to an actor. The scoreboard sums committed events; it never keeps a separate score state.

title: Live scoring rules · Holds and submissions
text: Hold/pin timers count down live and follow configured thresholds (e.g. 10/15/20 seconds). A tap or verbal submission instantly ends the bout and overrides prior points.

title: Live scoring rules · Penalties
text: Shido, yellow/red cards, point deductions and DQ ladders are configurable. Cards render on the correct fighter's side with a glyph; thresholds trigger the configured outcome.

title: Live scoring rules · Clock and stoppages
text: The server owns the clock. Referee stoppages pause it; the scorekeeper/moderator resumes. Overtime and golden score follow the rule snapshot.

title: Live scoring rules · Best-of-N and multi-round bouts
text: Best-of-three/five tracks each round separately, then applies the series rule. Kata rounds and bunkai scores are stored separately from fight scores.

title: Live scoring rules · Tie-breakers
text: An ordered chain resolves pool standings: wins, submissions, points scored, head-to-head, fewest conceded, fastest submission, positive play/majority as configured.

title: Live scoring rules · Medals across the whole programme
text: Medals are not limited to one fighting category. `awards.Reconcile` derives a deterministic podium for every category × discipline × event type present in results: JJ fighting, Ne-Waza/Katamewaza, Randori, continuous/sparring blocks and kata/weapon kata. Kata uses final panel totals; fights rank by wins then catalogue points. Gold, silver and one or two bronzes follow the configured format policy,

title: Live scoring rules · Result codes
text: `WP/LP/DP` (points), `WS/LS` (submission), `WT/LT` (technical/forfeit/injury/DQ/red card). W/L/D always show a glyph as well as a colour.

title: Live scoring rules · Simulated tournament scores
text: The global replay simulator uses the same technique catalogue as the officials console. Full simulated fights accumulate catalogue point values from strikes, throws, takedowns, holds and ground work, so typical totals finish in the 10–40 range. A submission is resolved from its catalogue entry as an instant win: the score may still be shown, but the tap decides the result regardless of who led.

title: Live scoring rules · Confirmation and undo
text: Major actions ask for confirmation. Results lock after confirmation; corrections are explicit audited undo events with before/after values.

title: Displays & screens
text: Multi-screen routes, themes, PA and custom views.

title: Displays & screens · Displays & screens
text: # Displays & multi-screen views  Every view has its own URL, so the control room, public dashboard and several full-screen boards can run on separate screens and stay live-synced.

title: Displays & screens · Core routes
text: `/public` dashboard, `/display` scoreboard, `/brackets`, `/tables`, `/pools`, `/control`, `/schedule`, `/medals`, `/ceremony`. In-app navigation stays client-side; use **↗ New tab** for a TV/projector board.

title: Displays & screens · What the scoreboard shows
text: Event title, mat, banner/logo, fighter names/photos/belts/stats, club logos or independent mark, officials with roles, per-side moves and cards, authoritative clock and recent technique callouts. Winners animate with configurable celebrations.

title: Displays & screens · Responsive layouts
text: Design range is 6" phone to 100" LED. Ultrawide screens use full width; phones get labelled cards, section tabs and explicit "show more" controls instead of horizontal or endless scrolling.

title: Displays & screens · Themes and branding
text: White-label tokens control colours, fonts, logos and banners. Corner colours and result glyphs are configurable; the Street Fighter theme is the default high-energy palette, with dark ink on its bright pink/orange/yellow fills so labels stay legible. Banners use `contain` so the entire uploaded image is visible against a themed backdrop.

title: Displays & screens · Navigation and fit
text: The desktop navigation is drag-resizable (180–380 px, arrow keys supported) and stores the chosen width; labels and spacing scale with it. The active view gets a bright themed left bar and glow, and the mobile drawer/bottom bar use the same treatment. The account switcher is clipped to the nav pane.

title: Displays & screens · Live event / Simulated tournament
text: The nav has an explicit **Live event / Simulated tournament** toggle (including compact and mobile nav). Live is the real venue state. Simulated mode is app-wide and persists in the URL and local storage; it shows a persistent replay widget on every view with play/pause, restart, previous/next bout, speed and full scrubbing. `/simulate` is the full event-by-event console and switches the app into

title: Displays & screens · Live invalidation
text: The venue server broadcasts cheap `state.changed` SSE frames after material writes: results, brackets and promotions, officials, kata scores/advancement, medals and schedule changes. Open brackets, officials console, scoreboard/mat/display, public, tables, pools, overlay, custom widgets and the medal ceremony refetch immediately on those frames instead of waiting for a poll interval. Fight scores

title: Displays & screens · PA and announcements
text: PA toasts flash fighter cards and call competitors to a mat/podium. Browser TTS speaks announcements; timed toasts auto-dismiss.

title: Displays & screens · Custom views
text: The builder lets authorised users drag/resize live widgets, save, clone, load and delete named layouts, and open them as standalone `/view` screens.

title: Displays & screens · Broadcast
text: A transparent OBS/vMix overlay and public live page are available; VAR/camera replay needs external streaming integration.

title: Developer guide
text: Architecture, commands, contracts and troubleshooting.

title: Developer guide · Developer guide
text: # Developer guide

title: Developer guide · Stack
text: Go single binary with pure-Go SQLite (`modernc.org/sqlite`), REST + SSE, OpenAPI contract; SvelteKit + TypeScript + Bun (never npm); Capacitor for iOS/Android. Types are generated into `web/src/lib/api-types.d.ts`.

title: Developer guide · First run
text: ```bash bun run dev          # venue server + web UI with seeded Okami 2027 data bun run demo:full    # full deterministic tournament seed bash scripts/dev.sh  # TUI menus for QA/build/mobile/docs ```

title: Developer guide · Project layout
text: `cmd/j3d` server; `internal/{api,auth,config,db,rules,seed,simulator,techniques,units}` backend; `api/openapi.yaml` contract; `web/` SvelteKit app; `scripts/` QA/build helpers; `docs/` guides.

title: Developer guide · API and generated types
text: Change `api/openapi.yaml`, then `bun run generate:types`. A Go test asserts route parity; a CI step fails if the checked-in types are stale. Docs indexes are regenerated with `bun run sync:api-docs`.

title: Developer guide · Adding a screen
text: Use existing route/lib patterns, keep role/phone guards in `web/src/lib/nav.ts`, add an E2E check, and keep W/L/D accessible with glyphs. Operator tools belong on tablet/desktop, not phones.

title: Developer guide · Live scoring rules
text: Clients send `techniqueId`/`pointLabel`; the server resolves points from the rule snapshot, enforces assignment and writes committed events. Visualisations query committed data and receive SSE updates.

title: Developer guide · Verification
text: `go vet ./...`, `go test ./...`, `go test -race ./...`, `bun run check`, `bun run test`, `bun run e2e`, `bun run build`, `bun run smoke`, `bun run load`, `bun run test:tui`, `bun run check:workflows`.

title: Developer guide · Troubleshooting
text: If API calls 401 in demo, the session may be stale — the client retries once with a fresh session. For mobile CORS use local demo origins `http://localhost` / `capacitor://localhost`. Check `docs/API.md` for auth and boundary examples.

title: CI & releases
text: Quality gates, workflows and release process.

title: CI & releases · CI & releases
text: # CI/CD & release process

title: CI & releases · Branches
text: `main` is protected. PRs run verification; release tags build and publish versioned, installable mobile clients plus production server/client artifacts.

title: CI & releases · Free-only hosted CI
text: No billing account, payment method or spending limit is required. Every job in every workflow has a job-level guard:  ```yaml if: github.event.repository.visibility == 'public' ```  GitHub-hosted runners are free for public repositories, and this repository is public, so the hosted gates run normally at no cost. The visibility guard remains as a safety rail: if the repo is ever made private again,

title: CI & releases · Automated gates (.github/workflows/ci.yml)
text: Go vet/test/race/build; Bun check/test/build; generated-type parity; smoke, load and Playwright + axe E2E; workflow syntax/TUI checks. All must pass before merge.

title: CI & releases · Mobile (.github/workflows/mobile.yml)
text: Every run:  1. regenerates the seeded Okami 2027 SQLite database and read-only API snapshot; 2. builds the web client with `VITE_OFFLINE_DEMO=1 VITE_QA_AUTOLOGIN=1` (first launch seeds the bundled data and signs in as the seeded admin); 3. produces an installable Android QA APK and an iOS simulator app; 4. boots an Android emulator and iOS simulator, launches each native client and uploads screens

title: CI & releases · Releases (.github/workflows/release.yml)
text: Release builds call CI and mobile, then attach exactly four download categories to the GitHub release: GitHub's auto-generated **Source code** archives, one hosted server executable (`j3-server-linux-amd64`), the production Android client (`j3-android-<version>.apk`) and the iOS simulator client (`j3-ios-<version>.app.zip`, containing the `.app` bundle). No QA apps, docs bundles, web archives or I

title: CI & releases · Environments (.github/workflows/deploy.yml)
text: Staging/production deploys are environment-gated and consume the release bundle. Hosted owner credentials come from `J3_OWNER_*`; never commit passwords.

title: CI & releases · Local build outputs
text: Local builds stage into a single root `build/` tree so QA, deployment and release candidates come from predictable paths:  ``` build/android/   demo APK plus the seeded SQLite file and read-only API snapshot bundled in it build/ios/       iOS demo assets and, on macOS with Xcode, the unsigned simulator .app build/web/       production web bundle (API contract, docs and licence included) build/web-

title: CI & releases · Local rigour
text: Run `bun run cicd` or `bun run test:tui` before pushing. `bun run qa:docker:full` boots the full seeded stack through a working Docker/Podman daemon (see `docs/DOCKER.md`). `bun run docs` rebuilds the documentation site; `bun run sync:api-docs` keeps the contract/guides/search index and shipped licence in sync.

title: Free hosting
text: Run production and staging on free Oracle ARM infrastructure with persistent SQLite.

title: Free hosting · Free hosting
text: # Free production & staging hosting

title: Free hosting · The short answer
text: Use an **Oracle Cloud Always Free Ampere A1 VM**. It is the only genuinely free-forever option that gives you a real always-on Linux server, a persistent disk for the SQLite file, a runnable Go binary, long-lived SSE and your own HTTPS domains. Render/Fly/Railway/Koyeb/Cloud Run either sleep, have ephemeral filesystems, cap free usage, or cannot run this Go binary without a rewrite. Cloudflare Pag

text: Release artifacts already include:  - `j3d-linux-arm64` — the headless Go server for the Oracle ARM VM (`j3d-linux-amd64` for x86). - `web/` — the production SvelteKit static client served by Caddy, including `web/openapi.yaml` (live API contract/reference) and `web/docs/` (organiser, runner, official, participant, CI, hosting and developer guides). - `j3-android-qa.apk`, `j3-ios-simulator.zip` (`

text: `bun run dev` → **Build & deploy ▸** gives a near-one-click path:  1. **Build release (server + web + API + docs)** — regenerates the OpenAPI contract and docs index, builds the production web client (with the API reference and guide site), cross-compiles all server binaries and writes `dist/`. 2. **Deploy to staging** / **Deploy to production** — packages `dist/` and uploads it using `scripts/dep

title: Free hosting · systemd units
text: `/etc/systemd/system/j3d-prod.service` (copy to `j3d-staging.service`, changing the name, port, paths and env file):  ```ini [Unit] Description=J3 venue server (prod) After=network-online.target Wants=network-online.target  [Service] Type=simple User=j3 Group=j3 WorkingDirectory=/var/lib/j3/prod EnvironmentFile=/etc/j3/prod.env ExecStart=/opt/j3/bin/j3d -addr 127.0.0.1:8787 -db /var/lib/j3/prod/j3

title: Free hosting · Caddy HTTPS + SSE
text: `/etc/caddy/Caddyfile` — `flush_interval -1` is essential for live scoring SSE.  ```caddyfile app.example.com { root * /srv/j3/prod encode zstd gzip file_server try_files {path} /index.html }  staging.example.com { root * /srv/j3/staging encode zstd gzip file_server try_files {path} /index.html }  api.example.com { encode zstd gzip reverse_proxy /api/* 127.0.0.1:8787 { flush_interval -1 } reverse_

title: Free hosting · Mobile client against the hosted server
text: Build an APK with the HTTPS API baked in:  ```bash J3_SERVER_URL=https://api.example.com bash scripts/mobile.sh build ```  The QA build still bundles the seeded SQLite database and read-only API snapshot, so it opens with data and signs in as admin on first launch. While online it reads/writes through `api.example.com`; if the service is unavailable it falls back to the bundled read-only snapshot.

title: Free hosting · SQLite backups
text: ```bash #!/usr/bin/env bash set -euo pipefail ts=$(date -u +%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ) sqlite3 /var/lib/j3/prod/j3.db ".backup '/var/backups/j3/prod-$ts.db'" sqlite3 /var/lib/j3/staging/j3.db ".backup '/var/backups/j3/staging-$ts.db'" find /var/backups/j3 -name '*.db' -mtime +14 -delete ```  Run nightly with a systemd timer and copy encrypted backups to OCI Object Storage (20 GB free). Use SQLite `.backup`/`

title: Free hosting · Caveats
text: - Oracle may reclaim Always Free compute that is idle for 7 days; real traffic avoids this. - Home region is fixed at signup. Choose carefully. - Single VM is a single point of failure; backups and monitoring are your responsibility. - Restrict SSH to your IP, keep `J3_OWNER_PASSWORD` out of source control, and use HTTPS everywhere.

title: CLI & TUI
text: Menus, demo commands, QA gates and mobile builds.

title: CLI & TUI · CLI & TUI
text: # CLI & TUI reference

title: CLI & TUI · Start here
text: `dev.sh` is the plain-language menu (arrows/Enter, q/Esc to go back). Numeric shortcuts work too. `bun run dev` boots the seeded full-stack demo; `bun run api` starts just the venue server.

title: CLI & TUI · QA and verification
text: `bun run smoke` (80 API/UI checks), `bun run smoke:full` (full-seed), `bun run e2e` (browser/axe), `bun run load` (200 concurrent requests), `bun run test:tui` (57 menu actions).

title: CLI & TUI · Build and deploy
text: `bun run build` builds Go + web + docs; `bun run release` produces release artifacts; `bun run cicd` runs the local CI/CD sequence; `bun run deploy` is environment-gated.

title: CLI & TUI · Mobile
text: `bash scripts/mobile.sh build` regenerates J3 icons, seeds the bundled database/snapshot and builds the APK. `install` starts the Pixel 10 Pro AVD (Android Studio SDK, `-gpu auto`) and installs/launches it. `url` prints the baked LAN URL.

title: CLI & TUI · Containerised QA
text: The **🐳 Docker QA ▸** TUI menu runs the container stack in `full`, `okami`, `clean`, `light` or `dev` mode. The same commands are available as `bun run qa:docker*` (see `docs/DOCKER.md`). `j3d simulate -seed 42 -fighters 50 -out snapshot.json` writes a deterministic tournament snapshot without needing curl or a running server.

title: CLI & TUI · Data and reset
text: `bun run reset` resets demo data; `bun run seed:full` creates the complete deterministic tournament. `GET /api/v1/demo/credentials` lists seeded accounts (password `demo`).

title: CLI & TUI · Troubleshooting
text: If the emulator crashes, check that the Android Studio SDK and AVD `j3-pixel-10-pro` are selected. If the venue URL changes, rebuild with `J3_SERVER_URL=...`. Logs and screenshots live in `docs/qa/`.

title: Containerised QA · Containerised QA
text: # Containerised QA demo  A full, repeatable J3 demo runs in containers: a seeded venue API, a static web front end with a same-origin `/api` proxy (SSE-safe) and a deterministic tournament snapshot. `scripts/qa-docker.sh` uses a **working** Docker daemon when available and otherwise falls back to Podman; an installed Docker CLI with no daemon no longer blocks the stack.

title: Containerised QA · Quick start
text: ```bash bash scripts/qa-docker.sh full          # or: bun run qa:docker:full bash scripts/qa-docker.sh url ```  Default URLs are `http://localhost:5173`, `http://localhost:5173/simulate` and `http://localhost:8787/healthz`. text: When a Compose provider is installed, `compose.yaml` is equivalent to the default `full` mode:  ```bash docker compose up --build # or: podman-compose up --build ```  The script is preferred locally because it works with Podman directly and needs no Compose provider. title: API guide
text: Authentication, boundaries and worked examples.

title: API guide · API guide
text: # J3 API  The machine-readable contract is `api/openapi.yaml` (83 paths, 87 operations). Generated TypeScript types live in `web/src/lib/api-types.d.ts`; regenerate with `bun run generate:types`. Route parity is tested in Go and CI.

title: API guide · Authentication
text: Bearer sessions are stored server-side. Public routes are health checks, public boards and registration. In demo mode (`J3_DEMO=1`):  ```bash curl -X POST localhost:8787/api/v1/auth/demo              # seeded admin session curl localhost:8787/api/v1/demo/credentials              # accounts, password "demo" curl -X POST localhost:8787/api/v1/auth/demo \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"use

title: API guide · Boundary model
text: - **Public**: event details, dashboard, belts/kata catalogues, schedule, results, medals, technique palette and simulation. - **Authenticated**: query API, uploads, check-in, imports, announcements, brackets and templates. Sessions re-read status and role on every request; suspended accounts and stale roles lose access. - **Per-contest**: fight mutations require assignment (admin/runner override);

title: API guide · Worked examples
text: ```bash # Seeded data and generated draw curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" localhost:8787/api/v1/demo curl -X POST localhost:8787/api/v1/demo/pools/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"eventId":"ev-okami","categoryId":"cat-adult-76"}'  # Score a technique (points resolved server-side) curl -X POST localhost:8787/api/v1/fights/ok-fight-01/event

title: API guide · Errors
text: `400` validation, `401` missing/stale session, `403` outside authority, `404` unknown target, `409` duplicate/conflict, `500` generic (details logged, not leaked).
